advisory.summary: Collection endpoints bypassed library access controls, exposing restricted library data.
note: GHSA-rxw2-h55w-ffmh. GET /api/collections/:id loaded the collection by
primary key and never called checkCanAccessLibrary, so any authenticated
user could read a collection -- name, description and full book metadata --
from a library they are not permitted to access. The fix (2.34.0) returns
404 to a user the library is not shared with; the owner still gets 200.
Marker and status both move on the fix, but the marker is what grades it:
the attacker receives 200 carrying the owner's marker on 2.33.2, so the
leak is confirmed by observed data flow, not inferred from a status code.
The attacker is legitimately unauthorized -- created with
accessAllLibraries=false and no libraries, it gets 403 at the proper
/api/libraries/:id endpoints. checkCanAccessLibrary defaults to true for
every user type, which is exactly why the provisioner sets it false.
The advisory's affected range names only v2.32.1, the version reported.
2.33.2 is the last release before the fix: its CollectionController.js
calls checkCanAccessLibrary nowhere, and v2.34.0's calls it three times.

checks.name: A user restricted from a library must not read its collection
